correctness.rationale: The weighted adjacency spectrum is computed by the \(2n\)-point discrete Fourier transform; a matrix trace inequality bounds the SDP and explicit rank-one/rank-two Gram factors attain it. At noncrossing parameters, trace equality forces the min-eigenspace and the unit-diagonal Fourier coefficients uniquely fix the Gram. An even-cycle cut has either zero or at least two uncut rim edges; two matching cut patterns attain both upper branches. A regular-polygon halfspace argument proves every nondegenerate hyperplane of the unique rank-two optimum cuts all antipodal edges and precisely \(2n-2\) cycle edges. Elementary monotonicity yields the two thresholds, strict additive gap and unique ratio maximizer. Four classes of separately implemented finite checks passed: 42 exact-rational integer optimizations, 156 spectral bounds, 156 Gram objectives and 2240 rounding outcomes. Analytic proof, not these tests, establishes all integer \(n\) and real \(t\).

value.rationale: The precise weight thresholds distinguish when the SDP ceases to be integral from when rounding of its unique rank-two optimum starts to return exact combinatorial optima. At and above the integer transition weight, every generic hyperplane produces an optimum even though the SDP gap remains strictly positive. This differentiates algorithmic rounding failure from relaxation nonexactness on a natural parameterized circulant/Ising benchmark, and gives an exact worst-gap instance and asymptotic ratio rather than a routine table lookup.
